title: 1. Hook: A Village Where Trees are Family
text: Imagine a village where children play not just with each other, but with the trees. Where elders say, 'If trees are there, then only we can survive.' Let's travel to a magical desert village from 300 years ago, where a little girl named Amrita lived.

content.title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Think Like a Villager
content.prompt: If a king ordered his men to cut down the oldest, most beautiful tree in your neighborhood to build his palace, what would you do? How far would you go to protect it?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Khejadi Tree
content.description: A resilient tree that survives without much water in the desert.

title: 4. Reveal: The Bishnoi Community and Khejadi Trees
text: Amrita lived in Khejadli village near Jodhpur in Rajasthan. The village got its name because of the many Khejadi trees that grew there. The people of this village belong to the Bishnoi community, who have protected nature for hundreds of years. When the King's men came to cut the trees for wood, Amrita and other villagers hugged the trees to protect them, risking their lives.

content.definition_summary: A community in Rajasthan known for their deep love and protection of nature, plants, and animals.
A desert tree found mainly in Rajasthan, known for surviving with little water. Its bark is used for medicines, people cook its fruits, and its wood is not affected by insects.

content.question: Why is the Khejadi tree so important in the desert?
options: It requires a lot of water to grow.
It can grow without much water and provides food, medicine, and shade.
It is only used for building kings' palaces.
It bears apples in the summer.

content.title: Desert Trees vs. Jungle Trees
content.mistake: Thinking that trees cannot grow in the desert.
content.correction: Many people think deserts have no trees. However, trees like the Khejadi have adapted to survive with very little water, developing deep roots and special leaves.

content.title: 6. Reflection: Your Special Friend
content.prompt: Amrita had a special tree friend she visited every morning. Do you have a favorite plant or tree near your home or school? Write down 3 things you observe about it.

content.title: 7. Connection: Timeless Movements
content.tip: The story of Amrita happened over 300 years ago, but it connects directly to modern environmental movements like the Chipko Movement (hugging trees to save them) in the Himalayas. The idea of protecting nature is timeless.

content.title: 8. Mastery: Become an Earth Protector
content.prompt: Draw a poster or write a short poem that encourages people in your city to plant more trees and take care of the environment.
